prompt:
You are a formal verification assistant. The following Dafny program fails Dafny verification.

=== PROGRAM ===
method twoSum(nums: array<int>, target: int) returns (index1: int, index2: int)
    requires 2 <= nums.Length
    ensures index1 != index2
    ensures 0 <= index1 < nums.Length
    ensures 0 <= index2 < nums.Length
    ensures nums[index1] + nums[index2] == target
{
    var i := 0;
    while i < nums.Length
        invariant 0 <= i < nums.Length
        invariant forall u, v :: 0 <= u < v < nums.Length && u < i ==> nums[u] + nums[v] != target
        invariant exists u, v :: i <= u < v < nums.Length && nums[u] + nums[v] == target
    {
        var j := i + 1;
        while j < nums.Length
            invariant 0 <= i < j <= nums.Length
            invariant forall u, v :: 0 <= u < v < nums.Length && u < i ==> nums[u] + nums[v] != target
            invariant exists u, v :: i <= u < v < nums.Length && nums[u] + nums[v] == target
            invariant forall u :: i < u < j ==> nums[i] + nums[u] != target
        {
            if nums[i] + nums[j] == target
            {
                return i, j;
            } 
            j := j + 1;
        }
        i := i + 1;
    }
}

=== DAFNY ERROR ===
program.dfy(12,18): Error: this loop invariant could not be proved on entry
 Related message: loop invariant violation

Dafny program verifier finished with 1 verified, 1 error

=== COUNTEREXAMPLE ===
At initial state: nums.Length = 7721, target = 0. At a program state: i = 0.

Analyze the failure and respond with ONLY a valid JSON object — no explanation, no markdown, no code fences. Use exactly this structure:

{
  "spec_element": "<one of: requires | invariant | ensures>",
  "proof_obligation": "<one of: initiation | preservation | bridge>",
  "diagnosis": "<explanation of what broke and why>",
  "repair": "<the corrected Dafny specification line that restores the intended behavior>"
}

Definitions:
- requires: the precondition that must hold before the method executes
- invariant: the loop invariant that must hold throughout the loop
- ensures: the postcondition that the method must guarantee on return
- initiation: the precondition does not establish the invariant at loop entry
- preservation: the loop body does not maintain the invariant
- bridge: the invariant and loop exit condition do not imply the postcondition

So line 12 is: `invariant exists u, v :: i <= u < v < nums.Length && nums[u] + nums[v] == target`

The error says "this loop invariant could not be proved on entry" - this is an initiation problem.

At loop entry, `i = 0`. So the invariant becomes:

This says there must exist a pair (u, v) where 0 <= u < v < nums.Length such that nums[u] + nums[v] == target.

So the issue is that the method's precondition doesn't guarantee the existence of a valid pair. The method needs a stronger precondition that ensures such a pair exists.

The fix would be to add a `requires` clause that states there exists a valid pair:
`requires exists u, v :: 0 <= u < v < nums.Length && nums[u] + nums[v] == target`

This is a `requires` issue with an `initiation` proof obligation. The precondition doesn't establish the loop invariant at entry.
